appended.cloudrun:
Follow these container best practices:
- Listen on 0.0.0.0 on the port given by the PORT environment variable (8080 by default).
- On SIGTERM, stop accepting new requests and finish in-flight ones before exiting.
- Make sure the process receives SIGTERM and exits promptly (PID 1 signal handling).
- Write logs to stdout/stderr, not to files in the container.
appended.containerfile:
Follow these container best practices:
- Use fully qualified image names (registry/namespace/name) for every base image.
- Pin base images to an explicit version tag or digest, never `latest` or an implicit tag.
- Pin base images by `@sha256:` digest.
- Use a multi-stage build so build tools do not ship in the final image.
- Keep the final image small (minimal or distroless runtime base).
- Run the application as a non-root user.
- Never copy secrets such as `.env` files into the image.
- Add a `.containerignore` (or `.dockerignore`) to keep secrets, VCS data and local dependencies out of the build context.
- Install dependencies from the lockfile (`npm ci`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`).
- Use the exec (JSON) form for CMD/ENTRYPOINT so signals reach the application.
- Copy dependency manifests and install dependencies before copying the rest of the source.
- Clean the OS package manager cache in the same layer that installs packages, in every stage that ends up in the final image.
- Declare a HEALTHCHECK for the service.
- Keep the Containerfile free of hadolint warnings and errors.
appended.kube:
Follow these container best practices:
- Set `runAsNonRoot: true` (pod or container securityContext).
- Set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` on every container.
- Drop all Linux capabilities (`capabilities.drop: [ALL]`).
- Use the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile.
- Run with a read-only root filesystem (writable paths as volumes).
- Set CPU and memory requests and a memory limit.
- Define liveness and readiness probes.
- Do not mount the service account token (`automountServiceAccountToken: false`).
- Provide secrets from a Secret (`secretKeyRef`), never as a literal env value.
- Reference images with an explicit version tag or digest, never `latest`.
appended.openshift:
Follow these container best practices:
- Make the directories the application writes to owned by the root group and group-writable, so it works under an arbitrary UID.
- Listen on a port above 1024.
- Declare the runtime user as a numeric UID.
- Do not make directories world-writable to work around permissions.
appended.quadlet:
Follow these container best practices:
- Enable the service at boot (`[Install] WantedBy=`).
- Restart the service when it fails (`[Service] Restart=`).
- Enable Podman auto-update (`AutoUpdate=registry`) with a fully qualified image.
- Keep application data on a volume (bind mounts need `:Z` on SELinux hosts).
- Pass secrets with `Secret=` (podman secret) or an EnvironmentFile, not `Environment=`.
- Declare a health check (`HealthCmd=`).
appended.update-bots:
Follow these container best practices:
- Keep base images updated: extend the repository's dependency-update bot (Dependabot or Renovate) to cover the Containerfile.
- Keep the dependency updates that were already configured.
- Keep the update bot configuration valid.

gates.title: Artifact
gates.description: A `Containerfile` or `Dockerfile` exists in the app directory.

gates.title: Build
gates.description: The grader removes the agent's containers and pods, then rebuilds the file with `podman build --no-cache`. The agent's own images are never trusted.

gates.title: Start
gates.description: `podman run -d -p 18080:<port>` starts the image (with the task's platform constraints, if any) and the container keeps running.

gates.title: Probe

checks.title: Honours $PORT
checks.rule: Listen on 0.0.0.0 on the port given by the PORT environment variable (8080 by default).
checks.why: Cloud Run (and Heroku-style platforms) choose the port and pass it in `PORT`; a hard-coded port is never reached.
checks.how: A second container is started with `PORT=9123` and must answer the probe on that port.

checks.title: Drains in-flight requests on SIGTERM
checks.rule: On SIGTERM, stop accepting new requests and finish in-flight ones before exiting.
checks.why: Instances are stopped with SIGTERM during scale-in and deploys; dropping in-flight requests shows up as user errors.
checks.how: A slow request is started, the container gets SIGTERM 0.7 s later; the request must still return 200 and the container must then exit on its own.
accepted: production server with graceful shutdown (gunicorn, uvicorn, ...)
checks.not_applicable: The task's app has no slow endpoint.

checks.title: Stops promptly on SIGTERM
checks.rule: Make sure the process receives SIGTERM and exits promptly (PID 1 signal handling).
checks.why: A PID 1 that ignores SIGTERM (a shell wrapper, or an app without a handler) is killed after the grace period, every time: slow deploys and no cleanup.
checks.how: Time of `podman stop -t 10`: under 5 s passes.

checks.title: Logs to stdout/stderr
checks.rule: Write logs to stdout/stderr, not to files in the container.
checks.why: Cloud Run collects stdout/stderr; a log file inside an in-memory filesystem is lost and eats instance memory.
checks.how: After a few requests, `podman logs` must mention the requested path.

checks.title: Podman-native file name
checks.rule: Name the build file `Containerfile`.
checks.why: `Containerfile` is the engine-neutral name Podman and Buildah look for first. `Dockerfile` works just as well, so this is reported for information and never scored.
checks.how: Name of the build file the grader found in the app directory.

checks.title: Fully qualified image names
checks.rule: Use fully qualified image names (registry/namespace/name) for every base image.
checks.why: Podman resolves short names such as `node` through `unqualified-search-registries`: depending on the host it may prompt, fail, or pull from an unexpected registry. A registry-qualified name is unambiguous everywhere.
checks.how: Every external `FROM` must start with a registry host (a component containing `.` or `:`, or `localhost`).
checks.not_applicable: The build uses only `scratch` or earlier stages.

checks.title: Base image version pinned
checks.rule: Pin base images to an explicit version tag or digest, never `latest` or an implicit tag.
checks.why: `latest` (or no tag) silently changes what you build on; an explicit version makes upgrades deliberate.
checks.how: No external `FROM` may be untagged or tagged `latest`, unless it carries a digest.
checks.not_applicable: The build uses only `scratch` or earlier stages.

checks.title: Base image pinned by digest
checks.rule: Pin base images by `@sha256:` digest.
checks.why: Tags can be re-pushed; a digest identifies one exact image, so the same Containerfile always builds on the same bits.
checks.how: Every external `FROM` must include `@sha256:`.
checks.not_applicable: The build uses only `scratch` or earlier stages.

checks.title: Multi-stage build
checks.rule: Use a multi-stage build so build tools do not ship in the final image.
checks.why: Compilers, SDKs and build caches bloat the image and widen its attack surface; a separate runtime stage ships only the output.
checks.how: At least two stages, the final stage does not derive from a stage that ran build steps, and it copies artifacts with `COPY --from`.
accepted: builder stage + COPY --from into a clean runtime base
checks.not_applicable: The app has no build step (the task spec sets `needs_build = false`).

checks.title: Final image within size budget
checks.rule: Keep the final image small (minimal or distroless runtime base).
checks.why: Smaller images pull faster, store cheaper and carry fewer packages to patch.
checks.how: Size reported by `podman image inspect` for the rebuilt image, against the task's `image_size_mb` budget.
accepted: any base within the task's size budget
checks.not_applicable: The task defines no size budget.

checks.title: Runs as non-root
checks.rule: Run the application as a non-root user.
checks.why: A process running as root in the container turns any application bug into root inside the container.
checks.how: UIDs of the running container's processes (`podman top <ctr> huid`); falls back to the image `User` when the container did not start.
accepted: base image whose default user is non-root

checks.title: No secret baked into the image
checks.rule: Never copy secrets such as `.env` files into the image.
checks.why: Anything copied into a layer is readable by whoever can pull the image, even if a later layer deletes it.
checks.how: Each task app contains a `.env` with a unique canary value. The grader searches the image filesystem and `podman history` for it.
accepted: explicit COPY of only the needed files

checks.title: Build context ignore file
checks.rule: Add a `.containerignore` (or `.dockerignore`) to keep secrets, VCS data and local dependencies out of the build context.
checks.why: Without an ignore file, `COPY . .` sends and copies everything: secrets, `.git`, local `node_modules`.
checks.how: A non-empty `.containerignore` or `.dockerignore` next to the Containerfile.

checks.title: Dependencies installed from the lockfile
checks.rule: Install dependencies from the lockfile (`npm ci`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`).
checks.why: `npm install` may rewrite the lockfile and resolve different versions; `npm ci` installs exactly what was locked.
checks.how: Node with `package-lock.json`: a `RUN` using `npm ci`. Python: `pip install -r requirements…`, `uv sync` or `poetry install`.
checks.not_applicable: No lockfile, no dependency install step, or a language without one.

checks.title: Exec-form CMD / ENTRYPOINT
checks.rule: Use the exec (JSON) form for CMD/ENTRYPOINT so signals reach the application.
checks.why: The shell form wraps the app in `/bin/sh -c`, which does not forward SIGTERM: `podman stop` then waits and kills it.
checks.how: `CMD` and `ENTRYPOINT` of the final stage must be JSON arrays.
checks.not_applicable: The final stage inherits CMD/ENTRYPOINT from its base image.

checks.title: Cache-friendly layer order
checks.rule: Copy dependency manifests and install dependencies before copying the rest of the source.
checks.why: If the whole source is copied before installing dependencies, every code edit re-downloads all dependencies.
checks.how: In the stage that installs dependencies, no whole-context `COPY .` may precede the install `RUN`.
checks.not_applicable: No dependency install step, or a language without dependency manifests.

checks.title: Package manager cache cleaned
checks.rule: Clean the OS package manager cache in the same layer that installs packages, in every stage that ends up in the final image.
checks.why: Package indexes and caches left in a layer add tens of MB that no later layer can remove.
checks.how: Every `RUN` that installs OS packages in the final stage, or in a stage it derives from (`FROM <stage>`), also cleans the cache (or uses `--no-cache` / a cache mount). Builder stages that are only copied from are ignored.
checks.not_applicable: No stage that ships installs OS packages.

checks.title: HEALTHCHECK declared
checks.rule: Declare a HEALTHCHECK for the service.
checks.why: Lets the engine report when the service is up but broken. Note: Podman's default OCI image format drops `HEALTHCHECK` unless built with `--format docker`; the evidence says when that happened.
checks.how: A `HEALTHCHECK` instruction (other than `NONE`) in the final stage.

checks.title: hadolint clean
checks.rule: Keep the Containerfile free of hadolint warnings and errors.
checks.why: hadolint encodes many community Containerfile rules (DLxxxx) and shellcheck findings in `RUN` lines.
checks.how: `hadolint --format json` on the Containerfile; no finding of level `warning` or `error`. Failing rule codes are listed in the evidence.

checks.title: runAsNonRoot
checks.rule: Set `runAsNonRoot: true` (pod or container securityContext).
checks.why: Pod Security Standards (restricted) require it: the kubelet then refuses to start a container that would run as root.
checks.how: Every container (including init containers) resolves `runAsNonRoot: true` from its own or the pod's securityContext, and no `runAsUser: 0`.

checks.title: No privilege escalation
checks.rule: Set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` on every container.
checks.why: Blocks setuid binaries and similar from gaining more privileges than the process started with (PSS restricted).
checks.how: `securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` on every container, including init containers.

checks.title: All capabilities dropped
checks.rule: Drop all Linux capabilities (`capabilities.drop: [ALL]`).
checks.why: Default container capabilities (e.g. NET_RAW, CHOWN) are rarely needed; PSS restricted requires dropping ALL.
checks.how: Every container drops `ALL`; only `NET_BIND_SERVICE` may be added back.

checks.title: RuntimeDefault seccomp
checks.rule: Use the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile.
checks.why: Filters dangerous syscalls; required by PSS restricted, and not applied by default on many clusters.
checks.how: `seccompProfile.type` is `RuntimeDefault` (or `Localhost`) at pod or container level for every container. Static: `podman kube play` ignores this field.

checks.title: Read-only root filesystem
checks.rule: Run with a read-only root filesystem (writable paths as volumes).
checks.why: An attacker who gets code execution cannot modify the application or drop tools; also enforces statelessness.
checks.how: `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` on every app container (not part of PSS restricted, a common hardening baseline). The pod must still pass the probe under `podman kube play`, which applies it.

checks.title: Resource requests and memory limit
checks.rule: Set CPU and memory requests and a memory limit.
checks.why: Requests drive scheduling; a memory limit contains leaks. Autopilot-style platforms inject defaults when missing.
checks.how: Every app container has `requests.cpu`, `requests.memory` and `limits.memory`.
accepted: requests + memory limit (a CPU limit is optional)

checks.title: Liveness and readiness probes
checks.rule: Define liveness and readiness probes.
checks.why: Without readiness, traffic reaches pods before they can serve; without liveness, a hung process is never restarted.
checks.how: Every app container defines both `livenessProbe` and `readinessProbe` (readiness is checked statically: kube play ignores it).

checks.title: No service account token
checks.rule: Do not mount the service account token (`automountServiceAccountToken: false`).
checks.why: The app never calls the Kubernetes API; a mounted token only helps an attacker move laterally.
checks.how: `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the pod spec, or on the ServiceAccount the pod uses.

checks.title: Secret provided via Secret
checks.rule: Provide secrets from a Secret (`secretKeyRef`), never as a literal env value.
checks.why: Literal values end up in the Deployment object, its history and every `kubectl get -o yaml`.
checks.how: The task's secret variable reaches the container through `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` or `envFrom.secretRef`.
checks.not_applicable: The task's app needs no secret.

checks.title: Images pinned
checks.rule: Reference images with an explicit version tag or digest, never `latest`.
checks.why: `latest` makes rollbacks and audits impossible: the same manifest can run different code tomorrow.
checks.how: Every container image reference has a non-`latest` tag or a `@sha256:` digest.

checks.title: Writes work under an arbitrary UID
checks.rule: Make the directories the application writes to owned by the root group and group-writable, so it works under an arbitrary UID.
checks.why: OpenShift's restricted SCC starts the container with a random UID that only shares the root group (GID 0) with the image. Files owned by a fixed user such as `node` or `1001` are not writable, so the app fails at its first write.
checks.how: The gate runs the image with `--user 40713:0 --cap-drop=all --security-opt no-new-privileges` and unprivileged ports starting at 1024; the check then POSTs to the task's write endpoint and expects a 2xx answer.
accepted: write only under /tmp or a mounted volume

checks.title: Unprivileged port
checks.rule: Listen on a port above 1024.
checks.why: Without the NET_BIND_SERVICE capability, which restricted SCCs drop, a process cannot bind ports below 1024.
checks.how: Ports declared with `EXPOSE` in the rebuilt image.

checks.title: Numeric non-root USER
checks.rule: Declare the runtime user as a numeric UID.
checks.why: Platforms enforcing runAsNonRoot can only verify a numeric UID; a user name is rejected because it could map to root.
checks.how: `User` in the rebuilt image's config: a number other than 0.

checks.title: No world-writable directories
checks.rule: Do not make directories world-writable to work around permissions.
checks.why: `chmod 777` fixes the permission error but lets any process in the container rewrite the application.
checks.how: Walks the image filesystem for directories with the other-write bit and no sticky bit, ignoring standard scratch directories (`/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/dev`, `/run`).

checks.title: Starts at boot
checks.rule: Enable the service at boot (`[Install] WantedBy=`).
checks.why: Quadlet units are generated at boot; without an [Install] section nothing starts them.
checks.how: A .container/.kube/.pod unit has `WantedBy=` (or `RequiredBy=`) `multi-user.target` or `default.target`.

checks.title: Restarts on failure
checks.rule: Restart the service when it fails (`[Service] Restart=`).
checks.why: A crashed container otherwise stays down until someone notices.
checks.how: `Restart=` other than `no` in the unit's [Service] section.

checks.title: Podman auto-update
checks.rule: Enable Podman auto-update (`AutoUpdate=registry`) with a fully qualified image.
checks.why: `podman auto-update` (with its systemd timer) pulls new images and restarts units, rolling back if they fail; it only considers units that opt in and reference a fully qualified image.
checks.how: `AutoUpdate=registry` (or the equivalent label) in a .container/.kube/.pod unit; for .container, `Image=` must be fully qualified.

checks.title: Data persisted correctly
checks.rule: Keep application data on a volume (bind mounts need `:Z` on SELinux hosts).
checks.why: The container is recreated on every restart or update; data must live outside it, and on Fedora/RHEL a bind mount without an SELinux relabel option is unreadable by the container.
checks.how: A `Volume=` targets the app's data directory; a host-path source must carry `Z` or `z`.

checks.title: Secret not in plaintext
checks.rule: Pass secrets with `Secret=` (podman secret) or an EnvironmentFile, not `Environment=`.
checks.why: Unit files are world-readable under /etc; `Environment=` also shows up in `systemctl show`.
checks.how: The app's secret variable is provided with `Secret=` or an `EnvironmentFile=`, never `Environment=`.

checks.title: Health check
checks.rule: Declare a health check (`HealthCmd=`).
checks.why: Podman runs it on a timer and, with `HealthOnFailure=`, can restart an unhealthy service.
checks.how: `HealthCmd=` in a .container unit.

checks.title: Update bot covers the Containerfile
checks.rule: Keep base images updated: extend the repository's dependency-update bot (Dependabot or Renovate) to cover the Containerfile.
checks.why: Pinned base images only stay secure if something proposes updates. A repository that already runs Dependabot or Renovate for its app dependencies should get the same treatment for its images.
checks.how: Dependabot: an `updates` entry with `package-ecosystem: docker` whose `directory` (or a `directories` glob) is the Containerfile's directory; Dependabot detects files named `Containerfile` as well as `Dockerfile`. Renovate: the `dockerfile` manager is enabled, not excluded by `enabledManagers`, `ignorePaths` or a disabling `packageRule`, and its file patterns (default: `Dockerfile`/`Containerfile` names) match the file.
accepted: Renovate dockerfile manager enabled and not ignored

checks.title: Existing update config kept
checks.rule: Keep the dependency updates that were already configured.
checks.why: Adding container coverage must not silently drop the application dependency updates the team relied on.
checks.how: Every ecosystem (Dependabot) or manager (Renovate `enabledManagers`) configured in the starting repository is still present.
checks.not_applicable: The task starts with no update configuration.

checks.title: Update bot config is valid
checks.rule: Keep the update bot configuration valid.
checks.why: An invalid config makes the bot stop working entirely, usually without anyone noticing.
checks.how: Dependabot: YAML with `version: 2`, and every update has `package-ecosystem`, `directory`/`directories` and `schedule.interval`. Renovate: the config file parses as a JSON object.

tasks.instruction:
The Node.js HTTP API in `/app` needs to run in a container. Containerize it so it can be built and run with Podman.

The API listens on port 8080 and answers `GET /health`.

# local development credentials - never commit or ship
DATABASE_URL=postgres://inventory:acb-canary-0be7d215@localhost:5432/inventory

version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "npm"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"

# inventory-api

Small inventory HTTP API.

```sh
npm ci
npm start   # listens on :8080
```

node_modules
.env
.git
*.md
Containerfile
.containerignore

version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "npm"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
  - package-ecosystem: "docker"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"

FROM docker.io/library/node:22-slim@sha256:43ac6c60b8f89723f746e8a92ce91abd5017e627ce1ddfe4238355d3a30b772c AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev

FROM docker.io/library/node:22-slim@sha256:43ac6c60b8f89723f746e8a92ce91abd5017e627ce1ddfe4238355d3a30b772c
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY package.json ./
COPY src ./src
USER node
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD ["node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))"]
CMD ["node", "src/server.js"]

tasks.instruction:
The Python (Flask) API in `/app` needs to run in a container. Containerize it so it can be built and run with Podman.

The API must listen on port 8080 and answer `GET /health`.

files.content:
# local secrets

FROM docker.io/library/node:22-slim@sha256:43ac6c60b8f89723f746e8a92ce91abd5017e627ce1ddfe4238355d3a30b772c

USER node

FROM docker.io/library/node:22-slim@sha256:43ac6c60b8f89723f746e8a92ce91abd5017e627ce1ddfe4238355d3a30b772c
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY server.js ./
# OpenShift runs an arbitrary UID in group 0: give the root group the owner's rights.
RUN mkdir -p /app/data && chgrp -R 0 /app/data && chmod -R g=u /app/data
USER 1001
ENV PORT=8080
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD ["node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:' + process.env.PORT + '/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))"]
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

tasks.instruction:
Set up the notes API in `/app` to run as a service on our Fedora server with Podman: it must start when the machine boots, come back if it crashes, and pick up new versions when we push them to `quay.io/acme/notes`. Put the files in `/app/deploy/`.

The API listens on port 8080, keeps its data in `/var/lib/notes` and needs the database password in `DB_PASSWORD`.

files.content:
FROM docker.io/library/python:3.13-slim@sha256:7c61056e61ac89e852de05f3dc6fa51a6dd2181797bceed46aa725dd7cb2cd3b
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY app.py ./
RUN mkdir -p /var/lib/notes && chown 1001:0 /var/lib/notes
USER 1001
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["gunicorn", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8080", "app:app"]
